items.prompt:
(1) A syringe reading rises from 6 cm³ to 27 cm³. What volume has been collected?
A. 33 cm³
B. 27 cm³
C. 21 cm³
D. 4.5 cm³ [1]

(2) Which value equals 5 × 10⁻³ g?
A. 0.0005 g
B. 0.05 g
C. 0.005 g
D. 5000 g [1]

(3) A learner reads water in an upright cylinder while looking down from above. Which change best improves the reading?
A. View the lower meniscus at eye level
B. View the upper meniscus at eye level
C. Read the lower meniscus from well below
D. Tilt the cylinder towards the viewing eye [1]

(4) An empty balance reads +0.20 g each time. Which statement is correct?
A. Correcting the offset removes systematic bias
B. Repeating the same offset removes the bias
C. Subtracting 0.20 g would increase the error
D. An average makes a zero correction unnecessary [1]

(5) Which is a suitable heading for a table column containing gas volumes measured in cubic centimetres?
A. Gas volume / s
B. Gas volume / cm³
C. Elapsed time / cm³
D. Gas volume / cm [1]

(6) Which is the SI base unit of mass?
A. gram
B. newton
C. kilogram
D. mole [1]

(7) Using K = °C + 273.15, which value corresponds to 15.00 °C?
A. 4097.25 K
B. 258.15 K
C. 273.15 K
D. 288.15 K [1]

(8) With other conditions controlled, collecting 20 cm³ takes 50 s at 20 °C and 30 s at 30 °C. Which conclusion follows?
A. Every reaction speeds up at any temperature
B. Both trials have the same production rate
C. The warmer trial yields more gas overall
D. The warmer trial produces gas more quickly [1]

(9) Which apparatus delivers one accurate 25.0 cm³ portion of solution?
A. A 100 cm³ measuring cylinder
B. A volumetric pipette
C. A 250 cm³ volumetric flask
D. A graduated 100 cm³ beaker [1]

(10) Why does a clear appearance not prove that a water sample is chemically pure?
A. Colourless solutes can remain dissolved
B. Dissolved impurities must make water cloudy
C. A clear filtrate contains no dissolved salts
D. A colourless solution contains just one substance [1]

(11) Why is a pencil baseline used for paper chromatography?
A. Pencil marks dissolve with the solvent front
B. Ink could produce additional spots
C. Ink stays fixed while the samples move
D. The baseline must travel with each sample [1]

(12) Salt dissolves in water but sand does not. After stirring both with water, which step separates the sand?
A. Evaporate the entire mixture
B. Decant before sand settles
C. Crystallise the dissolved salt
D. Filter the stirred mixture [1]
items.canonical_answer:
(1) C. 21 cm³ Subtract the initial reading: 27 − 6 = 21 cm³.
Distractor explanations: A: Adds the readings instead of finding the increase. B: Ignores the initial 6 cm³ already present. D: Divides the readings instead of subtracting them.

(2) C. 0.005 g A negative power of ten represents a fraction: 5/1000 = 0.005 g.
Distractor explanations: A: This is 5 × 10⁻⁴ g, ten times too small. B: This is 5 × 10⁻² g, ten times too large. D: This is 5 × 10³ g; the exponent has the wrong sign.

(3) A. View the lower meniscus at eye level. Eye-level viewing of the lower meniscus reduces parallax for water.
Distractor explanations: B: Water has a concave meniscus; read its lower edge. C: Viewing from below still causes parallax. D: Tilting changes the surface relative to the scale.

(4) A. Correcting the offset removes systematic bias A repeated positive zero offset is systematic.
Distractor explanations: B: Repeating a fixed offset does not remove systematic error. C: Subtracting the positive offset corrects an over-reading. D: Averaging repeated biased readings retains the offset.

(5) B. Gas volume / cm³. The heading names the measured quantity and its volume unit.
Distractor explanations: A: Seconds measure time, not volume. C: The quantity is gas volume, not elapsed time. D: Centimetres measure length; volume needs cubic centimetres.

(6) C. kilogram The SI base unit of mass is the kilogram.
Distractor explanations: A: The gram is a mass unit but not the SI base unit. B: The newton measures force. D: The mole measures amount of substance.

(7) D. 288.15 K 15.00 + 273.15 = 288.15 K.
Distractor explanations: A: Multiplies by the offset instead of adding it. B: Subtracts 15 instead of adding it. C: Omits the 15 °C contribution.

(8) D. The warmer trial produces gas more quickly. The same volume in less time means a larger average rate over that interval.
Distractor explanations: A: Two trials cannot establish this claim for every reaction and temperature. B: Equal volumes collected over different times imply different rates. C: The trials compare time to the same volume, not final yield.

(9) B. A volumetric pipette A volumetric pipette is designed to deliver its specified volume.
Distractor explanations: A: A measuring cylinder is less precise for this fixed portion. C: A volumetric flask contains a specified total volume; it does not deliver a 25.0 cm³ portion. D: Beaker graduations are too coarse for accurate delivery.

(10) A. Colourless solutes can remain dissolved Colourless dissolved material can remain visually undetected.
Distractor explanations: B: Dissolved colourless substances need not scatter light or cause cloudiness. C: Filtration removes suspended solids, not dissolved salts. D: Colourless mixtures can contain several substances.

(11) B. Ink could produce additional spots An ink line may introduce additional soluble dyes.
Distractor explanations: A: Graphite in pencil marks normally remains insoluble in the developing solvent. C: Ink dyes may dissolve and travel with the solvent. D: The baseline must stay fixed so distances have a common origin.

(12) D. Filter the stirred mixture. Filtration retains insoluble sand while the salt solution passes through.
Distractor explanations: A: Evaporating the whole mixture leaves sand mixed with the recovered salt. B: Decanting before settling may carry sand into the liquid. C: Crystallising before filtration traps sand with the product.

items.prompt:
(a) State the SI unit of volume. [1]

(b) A solid reference melts at 80 °C. Describe two features of a melting observation that would support a sample being relatively pure and consistent with this reference. [2]

(c) A mixture contains sand and a salt solution. Explain why filtration can separate the sand but cannot recover the dissolved salt as a solid. [2]

(d) Water is needed from a salt solution, and the salt is non-volatile. Explain how simple distillation recovers the water. [3]
items.canonical_answer:
(a) The cubic metre, m³.

(b) The sample melts over a narrow range, with its melting temperature close to 80 °C under the same conditions.

(c) Insoluble sand is retained by the filter paper, while the dissolved salt passes through with the water in the filtrate.

(d) Heating vaporises water; the vapour is cooled and condenses in the condenser; non-volatile salt remains in the original flask while the water distillate is collected.
marking_guidance: Part a: Correct unit m³ (1 mark).
Part b: Narrow/sharp melting range (1 mark).
Part b: Temperature close to 80 °C (1 mark).
Part c: Insoluble sand retained (1 mark).
Part c: Dissolved salt passes with solvent into filtrate (1 mark).
Part d: Water vaporises (1 mark).
Part d: Vapour cools and condenses (1 mark).
Part d: Salt remains because it is non-volatile, giving separated water (1 mark).

items.prompt:
(a) State the cylinder volume and thermometer temperature shown in the unkeyed instrument figure.

![Instrument scales](visuals/VIS-6117-1-01.svg) [2]

(b) Draw a labelled filtration setup to separate sand from salt solution. Label the filter paper, residue and collected filtrate. [2]

(c) Plot cylinder reading against reference volume using these pairs (both in cm³): (0,0), (10,10.2), (20,20.4), (30,30.6), (40,40.8), (50,51.0). Label both axes and draw a suitable best-fit line.

![Blank graph grid](visuals/VIS-6117-1-03-blank.svg) [3]

(d) Calculate the mean of three volume readings: 24.8, 25.0 and 25.2 cm³. [2]

(e) A learner views the cylinder meniscus from above on every trial. Explain a possible reading error and how to improve the procedure. [3]
items.canonical_answer:
(a) Cylinder volume = 36 cm³; thermometer temperature = 24 °C.

(b) The funnel holds filter paper; sand is retained as residue on the paper; salt solution passes into a beaker as filtrate.

![Filtration and distillation reference](visuals/VIS-6117-1-02.svg)

(c) Reference volume is on the horizontal axis and cylinder reading on the vertical axis, both in cm³. Plot the six pairs and draw a straight best-fit line through the pattern.

![Completed calibration graph](visuals/VIS-6117-1-03.svg)

(d) Mean volume = (24.8 + 25.0 + 25.2)/3 = 25.0 cm³.

(e) Viewing from above creates parallax: the apparent meniscus position is displaced relative to the scale, biasing the reading. Read the bottom of the meniscus with the eye level with it.
marking_guidance: Part a: 36 cm³, accepting ±0.5 cm³ for this drawing (1 mark).
Part a: 24 °C, accepting ±0.5 °C (1 mark).
Part b: Funnel containing correctly placed filter paper (1 mark).
Part b: Residue on paper and a vessel collecting the labelled filtrate (1 mark).
Part c: Correct axis quantities/units and sensible linear scales (1 mark).
Part c: All six plotted points within ±0.25 cm³ vertically and half a small horizontal division (1 mark).
Part c: Straight best-fit line matching the points, not a staircase or arbitrary curve (1 mark).
Part d: Correct sum divided by three (1 mark).
Part d: 25.0 cm³, with unit (1 mark).
Part e: Identify parallax (1 mark).
Part e: Explain that the apparent scale position differs from the true level, causing bias (1 mark).
Part e: Eye-level lower-meniscus reading as the improvement (1 mark).
